extracted.intended_audience: Editors at Springer Nature who handle manuscripts
extracted.subtask_description: A collection of editor-facing resources (flowcharts and template letters) to guide handling common editorial situations in Springer Nature journals, and linked e-learning courses on peer review, research ethics, plagiarism and similarity checking. Aimed to provide best-practice pathways rather than exhaustive rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of flowcharts and template letters for editorial situations
rubrics_metrics.description: Each topic has a flowchart and, where appropriate, template letters. These resources can be used as a guide for managing the situations according to best practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The course presents a list of topics where editors may encounter problems; each topic presents the paths a problem can commonly take with the best option for handling each situation outlined. Not dogmatic—intended as a solid foundation for managing common situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fundamentals of Peer Review — confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Fundamentals of Peer Review outlines the basics of the peer review process, including confidentiality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confidentiality is a core element of peer review practice and is taught as part of identifying and managing reviewer interactions and reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fundamentals of Peer Review — conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Fundamentals of Peer Review outlines the basics of the peer review process, including conflicts of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should identify, manage and avoid conflicts of interest when selecting and communicating with reviewers; this is a core topic in the course.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristics of a good reviewer and how to invite them
rubrics_metrics.description: The course explains how to identify the characteristics of a good reviewer and how to invite reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance covers what makes a suitable reviewer (expertise, absence of COI, reliability) and practical steps for invitation; also links to assessing reviewer suitability as part of editorial decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to assess peer review reports
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fundamentals of Peer Review explains how to assess peer review reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes principles for judging review quality (thoroughness, fairness, constructiveness, relevance) and how to use reports in editorial decisions; wording on the page is high-level rather than prescriptive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal Editors' Code of Conduct — standards and expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Journal Editors' Code of Conduct sets out the standards and expectations associated with the role of Editor-in-Chief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A linked course provides an overview of the Code; use the Code to frame editorial behaviour, responsibilities and ethical standards for leadership of a journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research ethics — ethics approval requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Research Ethics course covers ethics approval requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should check for appropriate institutional/ethics committee approval documentation when assessing manuscripts involving human participants or other regulated research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research ethics — informed consent to participate
rubrics_metrics.description: Research Ethics course covers informed consent to participate in research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should ensure manuscripts report appropriate informed consent procedures and documentation where human participants are involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research ethics — animal study requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Research Ethics course covers ethics requirements for animal studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should verify that studies involving animals report compliance with relevant welfare and approval procedures and include required statements in the manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research ethics — clinical trial registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Research Ethics course covers requirements for clinical trial registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should confirm that clinical trials reported in submissions were registered in an appropriate public registry and that registration details are included in the manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plagiarism — types and practical handling
rubrics_metrics.description: The Plagiarism course covers the different types of plagiarism that exist and the practicalities of using Crossref Similarity Check.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes how to assess text overlap detected by similarity-checking tools and how to take action on overlaps; aims to teach recognition of types (e.g., verbatim copying, mosaic) and appropriate editorial responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: IRR (iThenticate Report & Response) service — similarity report analysis and recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: The IRR service analyses the Crossref Similarity Report and provides editors with a recommendation for new submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This optional tool supports editorial decision-making by interpreting similarity reports and suggesting actions; intended as an advisory aid rather than an absolute rule.
